Vehicle: 0.1% DMSO



Keep lysis volume minimal to maximize final protein concentration

exps.experimentalProtocol:
**9.16.26 - Plate coating and media prep**

 

1 12 well plate coated in 100 ug/ml PDL in sterile H2O, 1 ml per well, in incubator at 37C overnight

 

DRG media and DRG culture media prepared per protocol

 

15% BSA in DMEM/F12:water prepared and filtered per protocol

 

**9.17.26 - Collection, BSA cushion neuronal enrichment, and culture**

 

Digest solution prepared per protocol

 

Total DRG collected from 6 mice and held in HBSS on ice, 1 mouse per tube

 

DRG dissociated per protocol

 

During dissociation:

Centrifuge cooled to 4C and brake and acceleration set to 3 (out of 9 for gentle acceleration/braking)

 

6 BSA cushions prepared

2 ml of 15% BSA DMEM/F12:water per tube

 

6 50 ml falcons prepared with 70 um strainers

 

After final cell suspensions obtained post trituration, cell suspensions filtered through 70 um strainers

 

Strained cell suspensions slowly layered on top of the BSA cushion in each tube, 1 mouse per tube

 

Centrifuged at 80 x g for 8 minutes at 4C

 

Each layer slowly removed via pipetting (NOT aspiration), with \~100 ul of bottom layer retained to ensure pellet was not removed

 

Pellets washed with 500 ul of sterile DPBS (NO resuspension)

 

Centrifuge at 1000 rpm for 5 minutes

 

Remove PBS carefully, leaving \~50 ul to ensure pellet is undisturbed

 

For resuspension, 2 tubes were combined

Resuspend first pellet of each pair in 1 ml

Transfer this suspension to second tube of pair and resuspend

Bring volume to 4.1 ml, resuspend

Plate 1 ml of final suspension per well

Each well of the three biological replicates will be dedicated to veh, 1nM, 10 nM, or 30 nM

 

Cells initially plated @ 1420

Cell number appeared roughly equal across and within biologic reps

Neuronal enrichment appeared robust; very few non-neuronal cells/debris present

 

Vehicle and PCI media master mixes prepared as below

Vehicle: 3996 ul DRG culture media + 4 ul DMSO

1 nM PCI: 3992.2 ul DRG CM + 3.8 ul DMSO + 2 ul 4 uM PCI stock

10 nM PCI: 3996 ul DRG CM + 2 ul DMSO + 2 ul 40 uM PCI stock

20 nM PCI: 3996 ul DRG CM + 4 ul 40 uM PCI stock

 

\~2 hours after initial plating (@ 1650), an additional 1 ml of DRG culture media containing either vehicle or PCI was added to appropriate wells

 

Cells incubated at 37C, 5% CO2 overnight

 

**9.18.26 - Lysis**

 

\~17 hours post initial plating, media removed from wells and replaced with 50 ul of 1X Laemmli buffer (4X Laemmli diluted 1:3 with 1X RIPA, supplemented with anti-protease and phosphatase cocktail and deacetylase inhibitor)

 

Disposable cell scraper used to ensure complete harvest from each well (fresh scraper per well)

 

Each well transferred to fresh 1.5 ml protein lo bind Eppendorf tube

 

Lysates boiled at 95C for 5 minutes

 

Tubes spun at 4C, 18,000 x g for 20 minutes

 

No pellet observed, samples flash frozen in LN2 and stored at -80C

 

**9.22.26 - Gel run, primary**

 

For each sample, 1.65 ul of 2-ME added to 31.35 ul of sample and boiled at 95C for 5 minutes

 

30 ul of each sample transferred to 4-15% TGX bio-rad precast gel

NOTE: 1 veh lane contaminated with ladder due to a collapsed well that went unnoticed until after sample had been loaded; do not trust for quant

 

Gel run started at 40V until samples exited wells

 

Voltage increased 20V every 10 minutes to a final 100V

 

Gel ran until 10 kDa at bottom of cassette

 

Transfer run at 4C (TGS HMW protocol)

 

Membrane blocked in 5% BSA 0.2% TBS-T for 1 hour at RT

 

Gel stained with IPS for 30 minutes

 Destained with milliQ for 30 minutes

![image.png](/uploads/67eaf447f188_image.png "image.png")

Membrane cut at 75 kDa

 

Membranes incubated in 1% BSA 0.2% TBS-T overnight at 4C

Top: acSMC3 1:500, Ms (millipore mabe1073, lot 4173169)

NOTE: not the usual MABE1925; too little stock. 1073 has worked in the past, relatively comparable to 1925 but marginally worse

Bottom: H3K27ac 1:500, Rb (abcam ab4729, lot 5/25/25)
exps.results:
Rep 1 veh well accidentally loaded into left ladder well due to collapsed gel wall. Attempted to salvage, but signal was too poor to use. This resulted in only two usable data points for veh. By column measure and peak selection method, saw no changes in acSMC3 or H3K27ac. By Ilaria's small rectangular ROI quantification method, saw a significant *decrease* in acSMC3 in the 10 nM condition relative to veh.

Decided to repeat with a pan class I HDAC inhibitor (MS-275) condition as a positive control for H3K27ac and to ensure that any effect seen isn't due to off target inhibition of other class I HDACs.

Additionally, the use of Anthony's PCI stock, which was over six months old, had been thawed multiple times, and contained 0.1% DMSO (far higher than necessary) likely contributed to these confounding results.

exps.results:
Low protein concentration only allowed 9.4 ug of total protein input per lane. The necessitated atto ECL to detect acSMC3, which created too much background on the membrane to reliably quantify most lanes. Will need to repeat with more protein input

H3K27ac was dramatically increased in MS-275 lane and unchanged in veh and PCI lanes. This result is clear and establishes that in DRG neurons, HDAC8 inhibition appears not to impact H3K27 acetylation, suggesting that HDAC8 does not primarily deacetylate histones in this context.

exps.name: SMC3 siRNA HDAC8i in vitro 1
exps.experimentalProtocol:
Conditions:  
	50 nM Smc3 siRNA  
		1 ul of 1 uM smc3 siRNA (1:100 dilution of 100 uM stock)  
	150 nM Smc3 siRNA  
		1 ul of 3 uM  smc3 siRNA (1:33.33 dilution of 100 uM stock)  
	50 nM scramble siRNA  
		1 ul of 1 uM scramble siRNA (1:100 dilution of 100 uM stock)  
	150 nM scramble siRNA  
		1 ul of 3 uM  scramble siRNA (1:33.33 dilution of 100 uM stock)  
	H2O  
	  
Each mouse: \~100k neurons  
Each nucleofection reaction: \~35k neurons = \~6-7 wells

Nucleofection -> 12 well plate for 72 hours -> replate into 24 well plate, add PCI 2 hours after plating -> fix 17 hours post replating

2 mice needed

SMC3 siRNA concentrations: 50 and 150 nM  
PCI concentration: 10 nM

10.12.2026 - PDL coating

5 wells of a 12 well plate incubated in 33 ug/ml PDL overnight at 37C

10.13.2026 - Tissue collection, DRG dissociation, nucleofection, and plating

PDL removed from wells and washed 3X with sterile water

400 ul of 2 ug/ml laminin in sterile PBS (1/500 from stock) added to each well and incubated at 37C 5% CO2 until nucleofected cells were ready to plate

2 male 11 week old BL6 mice (DOB 7/27/26) were sacrificed and total DRGs were collected and stored in sterile HBSS on ice

DRG were dissociated per protocol  
	NOTE: enzymatic digestion performed in heat block, NOT water bath (concerned that yeast survived in water bath despite three rounds of cleaning)  
	  
	All solutions thawed and warmed in sterile beaker filled with hot tap water, tube with solution placed in glove to maintain barrier between container and water

Cells counted with hemocytometer (\~3.0 ml cell suspension)  
	70k neurons/ml (210k total neurons)  
	\~490k total cells/ml (1.47M total cells)

Cells spun in large centrifuge 1000 rpm 5 minutes at RT

Supernatant pipetted off of cell pellet and cells resuspend in 1.47 ml of warm DRG culture media (1M total cells/ml)

250k total cells/transfection (1/7 x total cells = 35.7k neurons/transfection; 250 ul cell suspension)  
1 ul of siRNA or H2O per reaction  
20 ul P3 solution (16.4 ul P3 solution + 3.6 ul supplement per reaction)

21 ul total volume

Aliquot 250k total cells into each of 5 2 ml tubes and spin at 1000 rpm for 5 minutes at room temp (tabletop centrifuge by microwave)

Remaining media removed

Pellet of each tube resuspended in 19.4 ul room temp nucleofector solution (16.4 ul P3 + 3.6 ul supplement 1 per tube)

siRNA added to each tube  
	A (50 nM Smc3 siRNA): 1 ul of 1 uM smc3 siRNA  
	B (150 nM Smc3 siRNA): 1 ul of 3 uM smc3 siRNA  
	C (50 nM scramble siRNA): 1 ul of 1 uM scramble siRNA  
D (150 nM scramble siRNA): 1 ul of 3 uM scramble siRNA  
	E (H2O nucleofection): 1 ul of nuclease free H2O  
	  
Each mix transferred to a well of the nucleocuvette module, ensuring that sample covers the bottom of the well

Nucleocuvette placed into shuttle

Nucleofection program CO-113 (P3 solution) started on Amaxa nucleofector

After nucleofection program finished, nucleocuvette removed and cells resuspended in 80 ul warm DRG culture media for a final cell suspension volume of 100 ul

Cells incubated in nucleocuvette for 10 min at RT in hood

Additional 100 ul of DRG culture media added, cells resuspended, and transferred to sterile 1.5 ml tubes

800 ul of DRG culture media added to each cell suspension for a final volume of 1 ml

Laminin removed from each well of 12 well plate

Each nucleofection reaction was transferred to a PDL and laminin coated well on a 12 well plate @ 1500

Cells incubated at 37C 5% CO2 for 72 hours  
	Preps looked clean, some cell death from the nucleofection but typical, \~10%  
	Didn't notice anything that looked like yeast at time of plating  
	  
Plated remaining cell suspension (untransfected) in a separate 12 well plate  
	No PDL/laminin, so poor adherence. Serves as a control well for detecting potential yeast contamination

10.14.26 - Cell check

1X anti anti added to all experimental wells (all but leftover cell suspension in separate plate) proactively @ 1000  
	NOTE: media was NOT changed, anti anti added directly to existing DRG culture media  
	Hard to say if yeast present or not. Ilaria thinks no. Added anti anti (0.25 ug/ml amphotericin B plus pen/strep) to prevent any yeast present from entering replicative phase  
	  
Added ARA-C to 10 uM  @ 1000

Neurons appeared healthy, no issues with adhesion or stress/cell death

10.15.26 - Cell check and replating prep

Plates look clean, including holdout plate that did not receive anti anti

Added 13 mm coverslips to 2 24 well plates, incubated in 100 ug/ml PDL overnight at 37C 5% CO2

10.16.26 - replating and PCI/veh administration

PDL removed from replating wells and washed 3X with sterile H2O

500 ul of 1:500 laminin in DPBS added to each well and incubated at 37C until replating

Each well of initial 12 well plate trypsinized using 100 ul of 0.025% trypsin (1:1 in HBSS) @ 1800

1. Prepare M10 solution: DMEM/F12 + 10% FBS + 1% penicillin/streptomycin, place in beaker with hot water in glove
   a. 2 ml FBS
   b. 200 ul P/S
   c. 7.8 ml DMEM/F12
2. Remove DRG culture medium from wells and add 1 ml warm HBSS
3. Remove HBSS and add 100 ul of 0.025% Trypsin/EDTA solution (1:1 in HBSS from stock)
4. Incubate for 2-3 minutes at 37C
5. Gently tap plate on working surface of hood and swirl to dislodge cells
6. Check plate at scope for cell detachment (cells should move visibly when plate is gently tapped on the scope)
7. If cells are not detached, incubate an additional 1-2 minutes at 37C
8. Once cells are detached, add 1200 ul of warm M10 medium to each well
9. Pipette up and down gently, avoiding bubbles, to knock cells off plate
10. Transfer cell suspension to sterile 15 ml falcon tube
11. Add an additional 800 ul warm M10 media, pipette up and down gently
12. Add this cell suspension to the first
13. Check plate at scope to confirm cells have been removed
    a. If not, add additional M10 medium and repeat until plate is clear
14. Spin cells at 250 x g for 5 minutes at RT
15. Remove laminin from wells
16. Remove supernatant and resuspend in warm DRG culture media (2 ml, enough for 300 ul x 6 wells, roughly 6k neurons per well after replating)
17. Added 300 ul of each cell suspension to a PDL and laminin coated well of a 24 well plate @ 1845, distribute, and incubate at 37C 5% CO2
    a. H2O condition on separate plate
18. Allow cells to adhere for 2 hours in incubator
19. After 1.5 hours, prepare PCI and DMSO vehicle supplemented DRG culture media as below  ![image.png](/uploads/e7bca7adb479_image.png "image.png")

1. Add additional 300 ul of DRG culture media supplemented with either 20 nM PCI (for 10 nM final after 1:1 dilution) or 0.0002% DMSO (0.0001% after 1:1 dilution, same as PCI) @ 2045
   a. Cols 1-3: PCI
   b. Cols 4-6: veh
2. Incubate overnight

10.17.26 - Fixation and primary antibody

Fix at 17 hours post replating (@ 1145) (500 ul of freshly thawed 4% PFA, BRC stock prepped on 7.142026) for 15 minutes at 37C on slide warmer  
22. Wash 3X with PBS  
23. Block and permeabilize with PBS + 0.25% TX100 + 1% BSA for 1 hour at RT  
24. Wash 1X with PBS gently  
25. Primary antibody in PBS + 0.1% TX100 + 1% BSA leave overnight at 40C, covered with foil  
	a. acSMC3 (ms): 1:100 (millipore MABE1073, lot )  
	b. Total SMC3 (rb): 1:100 (CST 5696, lot 3)  
	c. TUJI (ch): 1:1000 (Novus NB100-1612, lot TUJ3947976)

10.18.26 - secondary antibody and acquisition

26. Wash 3X with PBS gently
27. Secondary antibody (usually 1:1000 glycerol stock) and DAPI (1ug/ml) in PBS + 0.1% TX100 + 1% BSA leave 1hr at RT
    a. DAPI 1:1000
    b. Rb 488 (total SMC3): 1:1000
    c. Ch 594 (TUJI): 1:1000
    d. Ms 647 (acSMC3): 1:1000
28. Wash 3X with PBS gently

customPhases.content:
Measures

Four measures to validate across manual quantification and existing automated methods

-

Neurite length (um)

-

per image

-

per neuron (for BRINE, manual, and any existing methods that can produce per-neuron data)

-

Number of branchpoints

-

Number of neurites

-

Percent of neurons with neurites

Image-level agreement metrics

-

Bland-Altman Analysis: difference between methods (M[BRINE] - M[manual]) versus average of two methods (M[BRINE] + M[manual])/2

-

Determines whether error scales with culture density or outgrowth extent

-

Lin's Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC): how closely a scatter plot of BRINE vs manual follows the line of identity (y = x)

-

\rho_c = \frac{2 \rho \sigma_x \sigma_y}{\sigma_x^2 + \sigma_y^2 + (\mu_x - \mu_y)^2}

-

rho is the correlation coefficient between x and y

-

overcomes limitation of Pearson's r that would mask consistent over/under estimation by BRINE

-

Intraclass Correlation Coefficient, two-way random effects (ICC(2,1)): whether BRINE's deviation from human consensus is within bounds of inter-observer variability (human vs human ICC)

-

-

k = number of raters

-

n = number of subjects (images)

-

-

(2,1) assumes raters are a random sample from a larger population and therefore measures absolute agreement. More appropriate than two-way random mixed effects (3,1), which assumes raters are constant and measures consistency

Passing-Bablok or Demming regression: assumes manual (x) axis has human tracing variance, unlike ordinary least sqaures (OLS) which assumes zero x-axis error

-

if 95% CI of y-intercept excludes zero, there is a constant offset of BRINE vs manual

-

if 95% CI of slope excludes 1, there is a proportional error, i.e. losing dim/thin distal tips of neurites

-

Distribution comparison (Earth Mover's Distance/Wasserstein Distance or KS-test): Compare population distributions of per-neuron neurite length to assess whether BRINE artificially truncates long processes at crossing points (shouldn't based on assignment logic, but need to validate)

-

Pixel level validation (clDice or buffered skeleton F1)

Number of branchpoints

-

Proportional Bias Check (Log-Ratio Bland-Altman): Branchpoint error almost always exhibits heteroscedasticity—variance increases sharply as arbor complexity grows. Plotting \log_{10}(\frac{\text{Auto} + 1}{\text{Manual} + 1}) on the Bland-Altman Y-axis stabilizes variance.

-

Overdispersion / Variance Ratio (\frac{\sigma^2_{\text{auto}}}{\sigma^2_{\text{manual}}}): Automated pruning thresholds can artificially compress variance (missing complex arbors) or inflate it via noise spurs.

-

Spatial Point-Matching (F_1** Score):** Image-level counts can hide compensatory errors (e.g., missing 10 true distal branches while inventing 10 false soma-adjacent spurs yields a "perfect" image count). If (x,y) coordinates are available, match automated branchpoints to manual ones within a tolerance radius (e.g., 3\text{–}5\text{ }\mu\text{m}) using the Hungarian algorithm, then report Precision (resistance to noise spurs), Recall (sensitivity to true bifurcations), and F_1.

Number of neurites (primary)

-

Quadratic Weighted Cohen’s Kappa (\kappa_w): Treated as an ordinal classification problem (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, \ge 5 neurites), \kappa_w penalizes off-by-three errors (3^2 = 9\times weight) much more heavily than off-by-one errors (1^2 = 1\times weight) while correcting for chance agreement. A \kappa_w > 0.80 indicates strong clinical/biological concordance.

-

Exact vs. Adjacent Agreement Rates (P_0** and P_{\pm 1}):** Report the percentage of neurons where Automated = Manual exactly (P_0), alongside the percentage within \pm 1 neurite (P_{\pm 1}). In primary cultures, human annotators frequently disagree by \pm 1 on short nascent processes near the soma boundary; if P_0 = 68\% but P_{\pm 1} = 95\%, the discrepancy is likely threshold boundary noise rather than a structural tracking failure.

-

Morphological Phenotype Confusion Matrix: Neurons are often categorized functionally by polarity—Apolar (0), Unipolar/Pseudounipolar (1), Bipolar (2), and Multipolar (\ge 3). Constructing a 4 \times 4 confusion matrix and computing Macro-Averaged F_1 reveals whether the automated method systematically shifts cells across morphological classes (e.g., classifying unipolar DRG neurons with a proximal T-junction as bipolar).

-

Zero-Inflation Audit (Sensitivity & Specificity at N = 0): Separate the ability to detect whether a neuron has sprouted (0 vs. \ge 1) from the ability to count how many processes it has once sprouted (1, 2, 3\dots).

Number of neurites (total per image/mean per neuron)

-

Square-Root Transformed Bland-Altman (\sqrt{Y_{\text{auto}}} - \sqrt{Y_{\text{manual}}}): Because count variance increases with neurite density, a standard Bland-Altman plot will show a "funnel" shape where Limits of Agreement appear artificially wide due to high-density images. Applying Anscombe's variance-stabilizing transformation (\sqrt{N + \frac{3}{8}} or simply \sqrt{N}) before computing Limits of Agreement stabilizes variance across sparse and dense fields.

-

Poisson / Negative Binomial Deviance & Dispersion Ratio: Compare the variance-to-mean ratio (Index of Dispersion, D = \frac{\sigma^2}{\mu}) of the automated counts against manual counts:

-

Over-dispersion (D_{\text{auto}} \gg D_{\text{manual}}): Indicates fragmentation. When an automated algorithm breaks long, dim neurites into disconnected segments and counts each piece as a separate "neurite," counts explode nonlinearly in images with long axons.

-

Under-dispersion (D_{\text{auto}} \ll D_{\text{manual}}): Indicates merging/saturation in dense fields where overlapping processes fuse into a single connected component.

-

Fragmentation Diagnostic (Correlation of Count Error vs. Mean Length): Calculate the Spearman correlation between Neurite Count Error (N_{\text{auto}} - N_{\text{manual}}) and Manual Mean Neurite Length. A strong positive correlation proves the automated tool is double-counting broken distal fragments as independent neurites rather than only counting soma-attached primary trunks.

Percent of neurons with neurites

-

Deconstruct the Ratio First: Always validate N_{\text{total}} and N_{\text{outgrowth}} separately before validating the percentage. If the automated pipeline undercounts total somas by 15\% and undercounts neurite-bearing cells by 15\%, the percentage will look deceptively accurate.

-

Cell-by-Cell Binary Classification (Confusion Matrix): On a subset of matched somas, classify each neuron as Outgrowth (+) or No Outgrowth (-):

-

Cohen’s Kappa (\kappa) & Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC): Measures classification agreement adjusted for chance—critical if your cultures have very low (<10\%) or very high (>90\%) sprouting rates where raw accuracy is misleading.

-

Sensitivity & Specificity: Reveals whether the threshold for calling a process a "neurite" vs. a membrane ruffle is too strict (low sensitivity) or too permissive (low specificity).

-

ROC / Precision-Recall Curve across Length Thresholds: If your automated tool defines a neurite-bearing cell via a cutoff (e.g., longest process > L_{\text{min}}), sweep L_{\text{min}} from 5\text{ }\mu\text{m} to 30\text{ }\mu\text{m} against the manual binary calls to find the exact threshold that maximizes Youden’s J statistic (\text{Sensitivity} + \text{Specificity} - 1).

exps.experimentalProtocol:
1.14.25 - Tissue collection and antibody binding

	1. Total DRG were harvested from 15 mice (5 etoposide injected, 5 vehicle injected, 5 untreated) in sterile HBSS in sterile, keratin-free 2 ml tubes
	2. In each condition, DRG were pooled as follows:
	1. 2 tubes of DRG from 2 mice
	2. 1 tube of DRG from remaining mouse
	3. HBSS was aspirated from each tube and DRG were flash frozen in LN2 and stored at -80C
	4. Washed 4X 50 ul of protein G Dynabead slurry (10004D, Invitrogen) in 1 ml of CHAPS lysis buffer + 0.01% SDS (w/o CHAPS, protease, or phosphatase inhibitors) (CHAPS LB (-)) 3X
	5. Incubated beads in 500 ul CHAPS LB (-) with 4 ug SMC3 antibody (Bethyl labs, A300-060A, lot 11) or rabbit IgG (millipore 12-370, lot 3974804) overnight at 4C with nutation
	1. 8 ul SMC (4 ug/0.5 ug/ul), 3X
	2. 4 ul IgG (4 ug/1 ug/ul), 1X

1.15.25 - IP

Where possible, all steps performed in cell culture hood with freshly prepared solutions to minimize keratin contamination
	1. Added 100 ml of CHAPS + 0.01% SDS + anti-protease + anti-phosphatase lysis buffer to pooled total DRG from 5 mice in each of 4 1.5 ml protein low bind Eppendorf tubes and homogenized with pestle on ice for 15 sec per sample
	2. Added lysis buffer up to 500 ul total volume and incubated for 1 hour at 4 degrees with nutation
	3. Centrifuged at 18,000 x g for 20 mins at 4 degrees
	4. Moved supernatants to new 1.5 ml protein low bind Eppendorf tube
	5. Determined protein concentration via BCA assay (ug/ul)
	ETP/SMC3: 2.8
	Untreated/IgG: 3.4
	Veh/SMC3: 3.0
	WB/SMC3: 3.0
	6. Collected antibody bound beads on magnetic rack and removed antibody solution
	7. Washed beads 3X in 1 ml CHAPS LB (-)
	8. Incubated antibody bound beads with 1.4 mg protein (added at 12:15) for 1 hour at 4 degrees with nutation
	ETP/SMC3: 500 ul
	Untreated/IgG: 408 ul
	Veh/SMC3: 468 ul
	WB/SMC3: 460 ul
	9. Collected beads using a magnetic rack and removed unbound fraction
	1. Unbound fraction flash frozen in LN2 and stored at -80C for downstream analysis
	10. For MS samples:
	1. Washed beads 2X in 1ml of cold (-, low) buffer + anti protease and phosphatase
	2. Wash 1X in 100 ul 1X cold PBS + anti protease and phosphatase
	3. Wash 2X in 100 ul room temp 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate
	4. Resuspend in 30 ul room temp 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate and bring to Liwen Zhang for MS
	NOTE: HeLA peptide standard added to all samples by MS core. Samples run anyway, attempting to throw out human peptides and keep only data from mouse
	11. For WB/SMC3 sample:
	1. Washed beads 3X in 1ml of CHAPS LB (-) + anti protease and phosphatase
	2. Added 30 ul of 1X loading buffer in CHAPS lysis buffer (+ anti protease and phosphatase) with LDS and 5% B-ME
		a. 7.5 ul 4X Laemmli
		b. 1.5 ul B-ME
		c. 21 ul CHAPS lysis buffer (+ anti protease and phosphatase)
	3. Boiled beads at 95 C for 5 minutes
	4. Spun down beads and collected on magnetic rack
	5. Eluent transferred to new tube and stored at 4C
		a. Didn't run blot immediately since there wasn't enough protein for and IgG control

1.17.25 - IgG binding for IP

	1. Washed 50 ul of protein G Dynabead slurry (10004D, Invitrogen) in 1 ml of CHAPS lysis buffer + 0.01% SDS (w/o CHAPS, protease, or phosphatase inhibitors) (CHAPS LB (-)) 3X
	2. Incubated beads in 500 ul CHAPS LB (-) with 4 ug rabbit IgG (millipore 12-370, lot 3974804) overnight at 4 C with nutation
	1. 4 ul IgG (4 ug/1 ug/ul)

1.18.25 - IgG IP for WB, gel run, blocking, primary

	1. Added 100 ml of CHAPS + 0.01% SDS + anti-protease + anti-phosphatase lysis buffer to pooled total DRG from 5 mice in a 1.5 ml protein low bind Eppendorf tube and homogenized with pestle on ice for 15 sec
	2. Added lysis buffer up to 500 ul total volume and incubated for 1 hour at 4 degrees with nutation
	3. Centrifuged at 18,000 x g for 20 mins at 4 degrees
	4. Moved supernatant to new 1.5 ml protein low bind Eppendorf tube
	5. Determined protein concentration via BCA assay (3.8 ug/ul)
	6. Collected antibody bound beads on magnetic rack and removed antibody solution
	7. Washed beads 3X in 1 ml CHAPS LB (-)
	8. Incubated antibody bound beads with 1.4 mg protein (added at 11:40) for 1 hour at 4 degrees with nutation
	9. Collected beads using a magnetic rack and removed unbound fraction
	1. Unbound fraction stored at 4C for downstream analysis
	10. Washed beads 3X in 1ml of CHAPS LB (-) + anti protease and phosphatase
	11. Added 30 ul of 1X loading buffer in CHAPS lysis buffer (+ anti protease and phosphatase) with LDS and 5% B-ME
	1. 7.5 ul 4X Laemmli
	2. 1.5 ul B-ME
	3. 21 ul CHAPS lysis buffer (+ anti protease and phosphatase)
	12. Boiled beads at 95 C for 5 minutes
	13. Spun down beads and collected on magnetic rack
	14. Eluent transferred to new tube
	15. Input and FT samples prepared as above
	1. Note: input prepared as above and 35 ul loaded of 36 prepared
	16. Gel loaded as above
	17. Run started at 40V until samples had left wells
	18. Voltage 20V every 10 min to a final voltage of 100V
	19. Ran until 10 kDa marker was at the bottom of the gel
	20. Transferred using transblot turbo (high MW protocol)
	Used individual membranes and pads, not pre made transfer packs
	1. Membranes activated in 100% methanol for 1 minute, then equilibrated in 1X transfer buffer for 3 minutes before transfer
	2. Pads equilibrated in 1X transfer buffer for 3 minutes before transfer
	21. Membrane blocked in 5% milk 0.2% PBST for 1 hour with shaking at room temp
	22. Membrane trimmed and incubated in primary antibody solutions overnight at 4C with shaking
	Antibodies diluted in 5 ml of 1% milk 0.2% PBST
	1. SMC3: 1:500 Rabbit polyclonal, Bethyl laboratories A300-060A, lot 11

1.19.25 - Secondary antibody and development

Removed primary antibody solution
Rinsed briefly 5x with 0.5% PBST
Washed 3x 10 mins with 0.5% PBST
Added 1% milk 0.2% PBST to membrane with 1:2000 conformation-specific mouse anti rabbit secondary antibody (CST 5127, lot 12)
Incubated for 1 hour at room temp with shaking
Rinsed briefly 5x with 0.5% PBST
Washed 3x 10 mins with 0.5% PBST
Membrane briefly submerged in Clarity ECL reagent before being imaged on Herson chemidoc
Membrane cut between 50 and 75 kDa markers
Top: 1:500 rabbit anti MED1 (abcam ab64965, lot 1035381-22)
Bottom: 1:200 mouse anti PP4 (santa cruz , lot )

1.20.25 - PP4 and MED1 secondary and development

Removed primary antibody solution
Rinsed briefly 5x with 0.5% PBST
Washed 3x 10 mins with 0.5% PBST
Added 1% milk 0.2% PBST to membranes with appropriate secondary antibody
	MED1: 1:2000 conformation-specific mouse anti-rabbit HRP secondary antibody (CST 5127, lot 12)
	PP4: 1:5000 H+L goat anti-mouse HRP secondary antibody (invitrogen 31430, lot YL381965)
Incubated for 1 hour at room temp with shaking
Rinsed briefly 5x with 0.5% PBST
Washed 3x 10 mins with 0.5% PBST
Each membrane briefly submerged in Clarity ECL reagent before being imaged on Herson chemidoc
Both membranes also exposed with atto ecl

1.22.25 NIPBL Primary

Top membrane cut at 250 kDa
Top half (>250 kDa) incubated in 4 ml 1% milk 0.2% PBST containing 1:100 mouse anti-NIPBL (santa cruz) at 4C overnight with shaking
MED1 blot incubated in 3 ml 1% milk 0.2% PBST with 1:5000 goat anti-rabbit H+L
NIPBL incubated in 3 ml 1% milk 0.2% PBST with 1:5000 goat anti-mouse H+L
Blots developed with regular ECL
NIPBL incubated in 3 ml 1% milk 0.2% PBST with 1:1000 Novus Rb anti-NIPBL NBP1-85110-25ul, lot A106772
MED blot incubated in 5 ml 1% milk 0.2% PBST with 1:1000 MED14 (novus rb NBP2-56318-25ul, lot R90103 old milk from June 2024)

1.26.25 Secondary and development

NIPBL (rb) and MED14 blots incubated in 5 ml 1% milk 0.2% PBST with 1:5000 H+L goat anti-rabbit secondary HRP for 1 hour at RT with shaking
Developed with regular ECL and imaged on Herson chemidoc

Use CHAPS 0.01% SDS lysis buffer mouse cortex sample (30 mg/500 ul)
Increased antibody to 4ug, held beads at 50 ul
	Per ﷟HYPERLINK "https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/10004D"invitrogen, beads can bind up to 30 ug IgG per 100 ul of bead slurry
Don't stain for DNA damage targets (not using tissue from damage inducing setting)
	53BP1
	MRE11
	ATM
Initially stain with conformation-specific secondary antibody
	stain again with regular H+L secondary to improve signal for low abundance targets
Keep low MW membranes for PPP4 and CDK5 staining (will need to use conformation specific secondary to avoid IgG interference; won't work for PPP4, mouse antibody, can try light chain specific but likely won't help)
	PPP4: 35 kDa (https://www.scbt.com/p/ppx-antibody-c-6)
		From Di Giovanni paper https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6600644/
	CDK5: 33 kDa (https://www.cellsignal.com/products/primary-antibodies/cdk5-d1f7m-rabbit-mab/14145)
exps.experimentalProtocol:
5/01/24 - Antibody binding and lysate prep

	1. Washed 50 microliters of protein G Dynabead slurry (10004D, Invitrogen) in 1 ml of CHAPS lysis buffer + 0.01% SDS (w/o phosphatase and protease inhibitors) 3X
	2. Incubated beads in 500 ml lysis buffer without SDS or anti protease/phosphatase with 4 mg of RAD21 antibody (AB217678, lot 103389-1) or IgG overnight at 4 degrees with nutation
		a. 7.66 ul RAD21 antibody (4 ug / 0.522 ug/ul)
		b. 4 ul IgG (4 ug/ 1 ug/ul)
	3. Added batch 8 BL6M3 mouse cortex to 200 ml of CHAPS + 0.01% SDS lysis buffer and homogenized with pestle on ice
		a. BL6M2: 30.1 mg
		b. BL6M2 IgG: 30.5 mg
		c. BL6M3.1: 29.7 mg
		d. BL6M3.1 IgG: 29.8 mg
		e. BL6M3.2: 29.3 mg
		f. BL6M3.2 IgG: 29.2 mg
	4. Added lysis buffer up to 500 ul total volume and incubated for 30 minutes at 4 degrees with nutation
	5. Centrifuged at 18,000 x g for 20 mins at 4 degrees
	6. Transferred supernatant to new tube
	7. Determined protein concentration via BCA assay (ug/ul) NOTE: incorrect standard dilution curve used. Samples were actually half as concentrated as indicated, calculated, and loaded for this experiment
		a. BL6M2: 8.7
		b. BL6M2 IgG: 9.0
		c. BL6M3.1: 8.5
		d. BL6M3.1 IgG: 9.4
		e. BL6M3.2: 9.2
		f. BL6M3.2 IgG: 10.2

5/02/24 - CO-IP

	1. Collected beads on magnetic rack and removed antibody solution
	2. Washed beads 3X in 1 ml CHAPS LB + 0.01% SDS (no anti protease or phosphatase)
	3. Incubated antibody bound beads with 1.5 mg protein for 7.5 hours at 4 degrees with nutation
		a. BL6M2: 172.4 ul
		b. BL6M2 IgG: 166.7 ul
		c. BL6M3.1: 176.5 ul
		d. BL6M3.1 IgG: 159.6 ul
		e. BL6M3.2: 163.0 ul
		f. BL6M3.2 IgG: 147.1 ul
	4. Collected beads using a magnetic rack and removed unbound fraction
		a. Unbound fraction stored at 4C for downstream analysis
	5. Washed beads 3 x in 1ml of lysis buffer (-CHAPS)
	6. Added 30 ul of 1X loading buffer in CHAPS lysis buffer (+ anti protease and phosphatase) with LDS and 5% B-ME per tube
		a. 7.5 ul 4X Laemmli
		b. 1.5 ul B-ME
		c. 21 ul CHAPS lysis buffer (+ anti protease and phosphatase)
	7. Boiled beads at 100 C for 10 minutes
	8. Spun down beads and collected on magnetic rack
	9. Eluent transferred to new tube and stored at 4C
	10. Performed second elution with 30 ul of 1X loading buffer 5% B-ME 7% SDS per tube
		7.5 ul 4X Laemmli
		1.5 ul B-ME
		21 ul 10% SDS
	11. Boiled beads at 100 C for 5 minutes
		a. Reduced time to prevent demagnetizing beads
	12. Spun down beads and collected on magnetic rack
	13. Eluent transferred to new tube and stored at 4C

5/6/24 - Gel run, blocking, and primary antibody

1% input (15 ug/1500 ug input) and FT samples prepared as above, boiled at 95C for 5 minutes, and stored at 4C
Gels loaded as above
	Used precast TGX 7.5% gels
Run started at 20V until samples had left wells
Voltage increased to 40V for 30 min
Voltage increased by 20V every 10 minutes until a final voltage of 100V was reached
Ran until 10 kDa marker was almost off the bottom of the gel
	Kept whole gel to preserve low MW region for CDK/PP4 staining
Transferred using transblot turbo (standard protocol)
	Used individual membranes and pads, not pre made transfer packs
	Membranes activated in 100% methanol for 1 minute, then equilibrated in 1X transfer buffer for 3 minutes before transfer
	Pads equilibrated in 1X transfer buffer for 3 minutes before transfer
Membranes blocked in 5% BSA 0.2% PBST for 1 hour with shaking at room temp

exps.name: Cohesin solubilization blot
exps.experimentalDesign:
Collect tot-sciatic from 8 male BL6 mice (ele secretome injection mice)
Lyse in normal CHAPS buffer 1 hr, collect soluble fraction
Re-lyse pellet in CHAPS + 0.1% SDS (10X from normal) 15 min, collect soluble fraction
Re-lyse pellet from 0.5% SDS in 0.5% SDS 15 min, collect soluble fraction
Re-lyse pellet from 1% SDS in 1% SDS 15 min, collect soluble fraction
Treat each soluble fraction as its own sample and run in one lane on gel
Stain for smc3 and histone H3, assess at which concentration of SDS most cohesin and H3 are solubilized
	This will tell us which fraction (or at least what % of cohesin we've been looking at in MS experiments so far)
If at 0.1% SDS, just increase SDS in CHAPS, do short lysis (15 min at RT with nutation) and then immediately dilute 10X to reach 0.01% for IP
If more SDS needed, run another titration with 0.1 or 0.5% SDS and increasing NaCl to see if slightly higher SDS + higher ionic strength is sufficient to solubilize, if so, adjust CHAPS lysis buffer accordingly and proceed with short lysis and 10X dilution for IP
	Alternatively, buy commercial nuclear IP lysis kit and validate at western blot level (SMC3 IP, stain for RAD21) and then at MS

exps.experimentalProtocol:
10.20.25 - Tissue collection and antibody coupling

Total DRG collected from 14 male BL6 mice (DOB 7.15.25, 14 weeks old) into two 1.5 ml protein lo-bind tubes, 7 mice each
DRG washed 2X in HBSS, flash frozen in LN2, and stored at -80C
	1. 1 mg of Dynabeads M-270 epoxy beads weighed into each of two 1.5 ml protein lo-bind Eppendorf tubes
	2. Beads washed 1X in 1 ml of C1
	3. 5 ug of antibody + C1 added to beads
		a. SMC3 (bethyl A300-060A, lot 11): 10 ul ab (5 ug, 0.5 ug/ul) + 90 ul C1
		b. IgG (millipore 12-370, lot 3974804), : 5 ul ab (5 ug, 1 ug/ul) + 95 ul C1
	4. 100 ul of C2 added to each tube and mixed by gentle pipetting
	5. Bead/antibody mixtures incubated at 37C overnight with nutation + shaking (500 rpm in small incubator)

10.21.25 Nuclear lysate preparation, IP, elution, gel run, primary antibody

Bead Preparation
	1. Antibody bound beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
		a. Unbound antibody fraction collected in separate 1.5 ml protein lo bind tubes and stored at 4C
	2. 800 ul of HB (NO tween 20) added to tubes and mixed gently manually
	3. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	4. 800 ul LB (NO tween 20) added to tubes and mixed gently manually
	5. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	6. 800 ul PBS (NO tween 20) added to each tube and mixed gently manually
	7. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	8. An additional 800 ul of PBS (NO tween 20) added to each tube and mixed gently manually
	9. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	10. 800 ul PBS (NO tween 20) added to tubes and mixed gently manually
	11. Beads incubated for 15 minutes at room temp with nutation
	12. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	13. Antibody-coupled beads resuspended in 100 ul PBS (NO tween 20) (100 ul/mg beads) and stored at 4C until use
Nuclear Lysate Preparation
	1. DRG thawed on ice
	2. On ice, add 100 ul of ice-cold 1X Hypotonic Buffer (1:10 10X Hypotonic in Sigma H2O) supplemented with DTT and Detergent (1:1000 dilution of each)
		a. Supplement with anti-protease/phosphatase/deacetylase
		b. For 1.5 ml
		a. 150 ul 10X hypotonic
		b. 15 ul phosphatase inhibitor
		c. 15 ul deacetylase inhibitor
		d. 1.5 ul DTT
		e. 1.5 ul detergent
		f. 1317 sigma H2O
	3. Homogenize with mortar and pestle for 15 seconds
	4. Add supplemented 1X Hypotonic Buffer up to 500 ul total volume
	5. Incubate on ice for 15 minutes
	6. Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 850 x g at 4C
	7. Remove supernatant and gently resuspend cell pellet in 1 ml 1X Hypotonic Buffer (no DTT or Detergent) by pipetting up and down several times
	8. Incubate for 15 minutes on ice
	9. Check small aliquot under scope to make sure cells are swollen
	10. Add 50 L Detergent and gently pipette up and down 3-5 times to mix
	11. Centrifuge suspension for 30 seconds at 14,000 x g in a microcentrifuge pre-cooled at 4C
	12. Transfer supernatant (cytoplasmic fraction) to new 1.5 ml protein lo-bind tube. Keep pellet (nuclear fraction) in original tube on ice
	13. Check small aliquot under scope to see if nuclei are released and intact
	14. Resuspend nuclear pellet in 200 L Complete Digestion Buffer by pipetting up and down 3-5 times
		a. Per sample:
		a. 193 ul digestion buffer
		b. 2 ul protease inhibitor cocktail
		c. 2 ul phosphatase inhibitor
		d. 2 ul deacetylase inhibitor
		e. 1 ul PMSF
	15. Add 1 L of the Enzymatic Shearing Cocktail to each sample and vortex gently for 2 seconds
	16. Incubate suspension at 4C for 90 minutes
	17. Add 4 L 0.5 M EDTA to stop the reaction
	18. Vortex gently on a low setting for 2 seconds and place on ice for 5 minutes
	19. Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 14,000 x g in a microcentrifuge pre-cooled at 4C
	20. Transfer supernatant (soluble nuclear fraction) into a pre-chilled 1.5 ml protein lo-bind tube
	21. Determine protein concentration of nuclear soluble fraction via BCA assay
		a. Nuclear lysates pooled, avg conc = 3.04 ug/ul. Total volume ~410 ul
SMC3 Immunoprecipitation
	1. Collected antibody bound beads on magnetic rack and removed antibody solution
	2. Washed beads 3X in 1 ml 1X IP Low buffer (no DTT, PIC)
		a. For 3 ml:
		b. 5X IP Low buffer: 600 ul
		c. Sigma H2O: 2400 ul
	3. Incubated antibody bound beads with 577.6 ug protein (190 ul) (added at 16:50) for 1 hour at 4 degrees with nutation
		a. Volume brought to 500 ul with 1X IP Incubation Low buffer (+DTT, protease, phosphatase, deacetylase inhibitor cocktails)
		a. For 500 1 ml:
		a. 5X IP Low buffer: 200 ul
		b. PIC: 10 ul
		c. Phosphatase inhibitor: 10 ul
		d. Deacetylase inhibitor: 10 ul
		e. 1M DTT: 1 ul
		f. Sigma H2O: 769 ul
	4. Collected beads using a magnetic rack and removed unbound fraction
		a. Unbound fraction stored at 4C for downstream analysis
	5. Washed beads 3 X in 1ml of 1X IP Wash Low buffer (+DTT, protease, phosphatase, deacetylase inhibitor cocktails)
		a. For 3 ml:
		b. 5X IP Low buffer: 600 ul
		c. PIC: 30 ul
		d. Phosphatase: 30 ul
		e. Deacetylase: 30 ul
		f. DTT: 3 ul
		g. Sigma H2O: 2307 ul
	6. 30 ul 1X Laemmli (diluted in 1X IP Wash Low buffer) added to each tube
	7. Tubes boiled at 65C for 5 minutes to elute
	8. Spin and place on magnet
	9. Transfer eluent to fresh 1.5 ml protein lo bind tube
	10. Beta mercaptoethanol added to 5% final v/v

2.26.25 - Tissue collection

	1. Total DRG were harvested from 14 mice (7 etoposide injected, 7 vehicle injected) in sterile HBSS in sterile, keratin-free 1.5 ml tubes
	2. In each condition, DRG were pooled into 1 tube
	3. HBSS was aspirated from each tube and DRG were flash frozen in LN2 and stored at -80C

3.2.25 - Antibody binding

	1. Washed 3X 50 ul of protein G Dynabead slurry (10004D, Invitrogen) in 1 ml of CHAPS lysis buffer + 0.01% SDS (w/o CHAPS, protease, or phosphatase inhibitors) (CHAPS LB (-)) 3X
	2. Incubated beads in 500 ul CHAPS LB (-) with 4 ug SMC3 antibody (Bethyl labs, A300-060A, lot 11) or rabbit IgG (millipore 12-370, lot 3974804) overnight at 4C with nutation
	1. 8 ul SMC (4 ug/0.5 ug/ul), 2X
	2. 4 ul IgG (4 ug/1 ug/ul), 1X

3.3.25 - IP

Where possible, all steps performed in cell culture hood with freshly prepared solutions to minimize keratin contamination
	1. Added 100 ml of CHAPS + 0.01% SDS + anti-protease + anti-phosphatase lysis buffer to pooled total DRG from 7 mice in each of 2 1.5 ml protein low bind Eppendorf tubes and homogenized with pestle on ice for 15 sec per sample
	2. Added lysis buffer up to 500 ul total volume and incubated for 1 hour at 4 degrees with nutation
	3. Washed 3X 25 ul dynabead slurry in 1 ml CHAPS (-) 3X for pre clearing, stored on ice in 1 ml CHAPS (-)
	4. Centrifuged at 18,000 x g for 20 mins at 4 degrees
	5. Moved supernatants to new 1.5 ml protein low bind Eppendorf tube
	6. Determined protein concentration via BCA assay (ug/ul)
	Veh/SMC3: 4.1
	ETP/SMC3: 4.2
	Untreated/IgG: 4.3
	7. Pre-clear 1.9 mg of each lysate in 25 ul dynabead slurry for 10 minutes
	Veh/SMC3: 463 ul
	ETP/SMC3: 451 ul
	Untreated/IgG: 445 ul
	8. Collected antibody bound beads on magnetic rack and removed antibody solution
	9. Washed antibody bound beads 3X in 1 ml CHAPS LB (-)
	10. Removed pre-cleared lysate from unbound bead slurry and transferred to washed antibody bound beads
	11. Incubated antibody bound beads with 1.9 mg protein (added at 12:40) for 50 minutes at 4 degrees with nutation
	1. NOTE: For future, IP for at least 1 hour
	12. Collected beads using a magnetic rack and removed unbound fraction
	1. Unbound fraction and excess lysate flash frozen in LN2 and stored at -80C for downstream analysis
	13. Washed beads 2X in 1ml of cold (-, low) buffer + anti protease and phosphatase
	14. Wash 1X in 100 ul 1X cold PBS + anti protease and phosphatase
	1. NOTE: For future, DO NOT ADD ANTI PROTEASE OR PHOSPHATASE TO THIS WASH
	15. Wash 2X in 100 ul room temp 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate
	16. Pipette off ammonium bicarbonate and bring dry beads to Liwen Zhang for MS

Samples prepped as above and boiled at 95C for 5 minutes
	1. Gel loaded as above
	2. Run started at 40V until samples had left wells
	3. Voltage 20V every 10 min to a final voltage of 100V
	4. Ran until 10 kDa marker was at the bottom of the gel
	5. Transferred using transblot turbo (high MW protocol)
	Used individual membranes and pads, not pre made transfer packs
	1. Membranes activated in 100% methanol for 1 minute, then equilibrated in 1X transfer buffer for 3 minutes before transfer
	2. Pads equilibrated in 1X transfer buffer for 3 minutes before transfer
	6. Membrane blocked in 5% milk 0.2% PBST for 1 hour with shaking at room temp
	7. Membrane trimmed and incubated in primary antibody solutions overnight at 4C with shaking
	Antibodies diluted in 5 ml of 1% milk 0.2% PBST
	1. SMC3: 1:500 Rabbit polyclonal, Bethyl laboratories A300-060A, lot 11

3.12.25 - Secondary antibody and development

Rinsed briefly 5x with 0.5% PBST
Washed 3x 10 mins with 0.5% PBST
Added 1% milk 0.2% PBST with appropriate secondary antibody to all membranes
	All rabbit primary targets: 1:2000 CST mouse anti rabbit conformation specific HRP secondary (CST 5127, lot 12)
Incubated at RT for 1 hour with shaking

exps.results:
### Next steps

	Lyse ~5 mice total DRG with CHAPS LB, then solubilize resulting pellet with blending buffer. Western both fractions for histone H3 and SMC3 to assess efficiency of chromatin solubilization with CHAPS
		if significant amount of H3 and SMC3 in pellet, will need to increase ionic strength and/or add SDS to CHAPS to get complete solubilization of chromatin for IPs
		This has been called into question since ETP DRG MS2 data showed no interaction of cohesin with MRE11/53BP1/ATM despite a more complete enrichment of the cohesin complex than ETP DRG MS1.
		However, yH2A.X is present in MS2 SMC3 samples, so it may be that cohesin only directly interacts with yH2A.X and this is cohesin's critical role in DNA damage repair
	Additionally, move to protein A-TurboID proximity ligation approach
		Add antibodies for SMC1, SMC3, RAD21 (all rabbit host) to lysate, then prot A-TurboID. After ligation period (will need to be optimized), streptavidin pulldown and MS.
		This won't show direct physical interaction, in contrast to co-IP, but it will give us a better chance to catch transient interactors. Since we're not trying to establish regulatory roles at this stage, co-IP is overkill and we want to cast a broader net.
		If MS2 results are repeatable and we show that CHAPS is able to effectively solubilize chromatin (which would mean we're not just looking at cytosolic/easily accessible cohesin), then IP yH2A.X in WT and cohesin KO conditions and look for decreased interaction of yH2A.X with MRE11/53BP1 etc (repairosome). In concert with TurboID data showing cohesin is in close proximity to repairosome, co-IP data showing direct interaction with yH2A.X, should be enough to establish critical role of cohesin in repairosome recruitment/activation
MS-MS Results

exps.experimentalProtocol:
9.8.25 Antibody binding

	1. Washed 3X 50 ul of protein G Dynabead slurry (10004D, Invitrogen) in 1 ml of CHAPS lysis buffer + 0.01% SDS (w/o CHAPS, protease, or phosphatase inhibitors) (CHAPS LB (-)) 3X
	2. Incubated beads in 500 ul CHAPS LB (-) with 4 ug SMC3 antibody (Bethyl labs, A300-060A, lot 11) or rabbit IgG (millipore 12-370, lot 3974804) overnight at 4C with nutation
		a. 8 ul SMC (4 ug/0.5 ug/ul), 1X
		b. 4 ul IgG (4 ug/1 ug/ul), 1X

9.9.25 - DRG collection, kit lysis, IP, western blot day 1 (gel run and primary antibody)

	1. 1x 1.5 ml protein lo bind with HBSS
	2. 10X Hypotonic
	3. Digestion buffer
	4. DTT
	5. Detergent
	6. Complete Digestion Buffer
	7. Enzymatic shearing cocktail
	8. EDTA
	9. 5X IP Low buffer (no detergent or salt added)
	10. Total DRG collected from 10 male BL6 mice (DOB 7.15.25 ) and pooled in pre-weighed 1.5 ml protein lo-bind tubes containing 1 ml HBSS on ice (5 mice total DRG per tube)
	11. Determine sample mass
	12. Wash DRG 1X in 1 ml HBSS, draw off supernatant
	13. On ice, add 100 ul of ice-cold 1X Hypotonic Buffer (1:10 10X Hypotonic in Sigma H2O) supplemented with DTT and Detergent (1:1000 dilution of each)
	14. Homogenize with mortar and pestle for 15 seconds
	15. Add supplemented 1X Hypotonic Buffer up to 500 ul total volume
	16. Incubate on ice for 15 minutes
	17. Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 850 x g at 4C
	18. Remove supernatant and gently resuspend cell pellet in 1 ml 1X Hypotonic Buffer (no DTT or Detergent) by pipetting up and down several times
	19. Incubate for 15 minutes on ice
	20. Check small aliquot under scope to make sure cells are swollen
	21. Add 50 L Detergent and gently pipette up and down 3-5 times to mix
	22. Centrifuge suspension for 30 seconds at 14,000 x g in a microcentrifuge pre-cooled at 4C
	23. Transfer supernatant (cytoplasmic fraction) to new 1.5 ml protein lo-bind tube. Keep pellet (nuclear fraction) in original tube on ice
	24. Check small aliquot under scope to see if nuclei are released and intact
	25. Resuspend nuclear pellet in 200 L Complete Digestion Buffer by pipetting up and down 3-5 times
		a. Per sample:
		a. 193 ul digestion buffer
		b. 2 ul protease inhibitor cocktail
		c. 2 ul phosphatase inhibitor
		d. 2 ul deacetylase inhibitor
		e. 1 ul PMSF
	26. Add 1 L of the Enzymatic Shearing Cocktail and vortex gently for 2 seconds
	27. Incubate suspension at 4C for 90 minutes
	28. Add 4 L 0.5 M EDTA to stop the reaction
	29. Vortex gently on a low setting for 2 seconds and place on ice for 5 minutes
	30. Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 14,000 x g in a microcentrifuge pre-cooled at 4C
	31. Transfer supernatant (soluble nuclear fraction) into a pre-chilled 1.5 ml protein lo-bind tube
	32. Determine protein concentration of nuclear soluble fraction via BCA assay
		a. Eluents pooled, avg conc = 1.56 ug/ul. Total volume ~430 ul
	33. Resuspend pellet (insoluble nuclear fraction) in 100 ul of 1X Laemmli buffer supplemented with 5% B-ME and boil for 5 minutes at 95C
		a. NOTE: for future experiments, split this pellet in two, one for WB, one for agarose gel analysis of DNA fragmentation
	34. Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 14,000 x g in a microcentrifuge pre-cooled at 4C
	35. Transfer supernatant (insoluble nuclear fraction) to clean 1.5 ml protein lo-bind tube
	36. Discard pellet (cell membrane and ECM debris)
	IP
	37. Collected antibody bound beads on magnetic rack and removed antibody solution
	38. Washed beads 3X in 1 ml 1X IP Low buffer (no DTT, PIC)
		a. For 3 ml:
		b. 5X IP Low buffer: 600 ul
		c. Sigma H2O: 2400 ul
	39. Incubated antibody bound beads with 330 ug protein (215 ul) (added at 17:35) for 1 hour at 4 degrees with nutation
	40. Volume brought to 500 ul with 1X IP Incubation Low buffer (+DTT, protease inhibitor cocktail)
		a. For 500 ul:
		a. 5X IP Low buffer: 100 ul
		b. PIC: 2.5 ul
		c. 1M DTT: 0.5 ul
		d. Sigma H2O: 397 ul
	41. Collected beads using a magnetic rack and removed unbound fraction
		a. Unbound fraction stored at 4C for downstream analysis
	42. Washed beads 3 x in 1ml of 1X IP Wash Low buffer (+DTT, protease inhibitor cocktail)
		a. For 3 ml:
		b. 5X IP Low buffer: 600 ul
		c. PIC: 6 ul
		d. 1M DTT: 3 ul
		e. Sigma H2O: 2391 ul
	43. Added 30 ul of 1X loading buffer in CHAPS lysis buffer (- CHAPS, + anti protease and phosphatase) with LDS and 5% B-ME per tube
		a. 7.5 ul 4X Laemmli
		b. 1.5 ul B-ME
		c. 21 ul CHAPS lysis buffer (+ anti protease and phosphatase)
	44. Boiled beads at 95 C for 5 minutes
	45. Spun down beads and collected on magnetic rack
	46. Eluent transferred to new tube and stored at 4C
	47. Prepare 1 sample per fraction for western blot
		a. Flow through (FT): 5% of input (25 ul FT, 10 ul 4X Laemmli, 2 ul 2-ME, 3 ul 1X IP Low buffer)
	48. TGX 4-15% gel loaded and started at 40V until samples left wells
	49. Voltage increased 20V every 10 minutes to a final 100V
	50. Gel run stopped when dye front was almost at bottom of gel
	51. Transferred gel to PVDF membrane using high MW protocol on transblot turbo
	52. Membrane blocked in 5% milk 0.2% PBST for 1 hour with shaking at room temp
	53. Membrane trimmed and cut at 50 kDa, and membrane sections incubated in primary antibody solutions overnight at 4C with shaking
		a. Antibodies diluted in 5 ml of 1% milk 0.2% PBST
		b. SMC3: 1:500 Rabbit polyclonal, Bethyl laboratories A300-060A, lot 11
		c. Histone H3: 1:1000 rabbit polyclonal, cell signaling 9715, lot 24

	1. Membranes rinsed briefly 5X with 0.5% PBST
	2. Washed 1X 5 mins with 0.5% PBST
	3. Added 5 ml 1% milk 0.2% PBST with appropriate secondary antibody to all membranes
		a. All targets: 1:5000 thermo goat anti rabbit H+L HRP secondary

exps.experimentalProtocol:
2.1.26 -Antibody coupling

	1. 1 mg of Dynabeads M-270 epoxy beads weighed into each of two 1.5 ml protein lo-bind Eppendorf tubes
	2. Beads washed 1X in 1 ml of C1
	3. 5 ug of antibody + C1 added to beads
		a. SMC3 (bethyl A300-060A, lot 11): 10 ul ab (5 ug, 0.5 ug/ul) + 90 ul C1
		b. IgG (millipore 12-370, lot 3974804), : 5 ul ab (5 ug, 1 ug/ul) + 95 ul C1
	4. 100 ul of C2 added to each tube and mixed by gentle pipetting
	5. Bead/antibody mixtures incubated at 37C overnight with nutation + shaking (500 rpm in small incubator)

2.2.26 Nuclear lysate preparation, IP, elution, gel run, primary antibody

Bead Preparation
	1. Antibody bound beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
		a. Unbound antibody fraction collected in separate 1.5 ml protein lo bind tubes and stored at 4C
	2. 800 ul of HB (NO tween 20) added to tubes and mixed gently manually
	3. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	4. 800 ul LB (NO tween 20) added to tubes and mixed gently manually
	5. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	6. 800 ul PBS (NO tween 20) added to each tube and mixed gently manually
	7. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	8. An additional 800 ul of PBS (NO tween 20) added to each tube and mixed gently manually
	9. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	10. 800 ul PBS (NO tween 20) added to tubes and mixed gently manually
	11. Beads incubated for 15 minutes at room temp with nutation
	12. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	13. Antibody-coupled beads resuspended in 100 ul PBS (NO tween 20) (100 ul/mg beads) and stored at 4C until use
Nuclear Lysate Preparation
	1. DRG thawed on ice
	2. On ice, add 100 ul of ice-cold 1X Hypotonic Buffer (1:10 10X Hypotonic in Sigma H2O) supplemented with DTT and Detergent (1:1000 dilution of each)
		a. Supplement with anti-protease/phosphatase/deacetylase
		b. For 1.5 ml
		a. 150 ul 10X hypotonic
		b. 15 ul phosphatase inhibitor
		c. 15 ul deacetylase inhibitor
		d. 1.5 ul DTT
		e. 1.5 ul detergent
		f. 1317 sigma H2O
	3. Homogenize with mortar and pestle for 15 seconds
	4. Add supplemented 1X Hypotonic Buffer up to 500 ul total volume
	5. Incubate on ice for 15 minutes
	6. Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 850 x g at 4C
	7. Remove supernatant and gently resuspend cell pellet in 1 ml 1X Hypotonic Buffer (no DTT or Detergent) by pipetting up and down several times
	8. Incubate for 15 minutes on ice
	9. Check small aliquot under scope to make sure cells are swollen
	10. Add 50 L Detergent and gently pipette up and down 3-5 times to mix
	11. Centrifuge suspension for 30 seconds at 14,000 x g in a microcentrifuge pre-cooled at 4C
	12. Transfer supernatant (cytoplasmic fraction) to new 1.5 ml protein lo-bind tube. Keep pellet (nuclear fraction) in original tube on ice
	13. Check small aliquot under scope to see if nuclei are released and intact
	14. Resuspend nuclear pellet in 200 L Complete Digestion Buffer by pipetting up and down 3-5 times
		a. Per sample:
		a. 193 ul digestion buffer
		b. 2 ul protease inhibitor cocktail
		c. 2 ul phosphatase inhibitor
		d. 2 ul deacetylase inhibitor
		e. 1 ul PMSF
	15. Add 1 L of the Enzymatic Shearing Cocktail to each sample and vortex gently for 2 seconds
	16. Incubate suspension at 4C for 90 minutes
	17. Add 4 L 0.5 M EDTA to stop the reaction
	18. Vortex gently on a low setting for 2 seconds and place on ice for 5 minutes
	19. Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 14,000 x g in a microcentrifuge pre-cooled at 4C
	20. Transfer supernatant (soluble nuclear fraction) into a pre-chilled 1.5 ml protein lo-bind tube
	21. Determine protein concentration of nuclear soluble fraction via BCA assay
		a. Nuclear lysates pooled, avg conc = 3.04 ug/ul. Total volume ~410 ul
SMC3 Immunoprecipitation
	1. Collected antibody bound beads on magnetic rack and removed antibody solution
	2. Washed beads 3X in 1 ml 1X IP Low buffer (no DTT, PIC)
		a. For 3 ml:
		b. 5X IP Low buffer: 600 ul
		c. Sigma H2O: 2400 ul
	3. Incubated antibody bound beads with 577.6 ug protein (190 ul) (added at 16:50) for 1 hour at 4 degrees with nutation
		a. Volume brought to 500 ul with 1X IP Incubation Low buffer (+DTT, protease, phosphatase, deacetylase inhibitor cocktails)
		a. For 500 1 ml:
		a. 5X IP Low buffer: 200 ul
		b. PIC: 10 ul
		c. Phosphatase inhibitor: 10 ul
		d. Deacetylase inhibitor: 10 ul
		e. 1M DTT: 1 ul
		f. Sigma H2O: 769 ul
	4. Collected beads using a magnetic rack and removed unbound fraction
		a. Unbound fraction stored at 4C for downstream analysis
	5. Washed beads 3 X in 1ml of 1X IP Wash Low buffer (+DTT, protease, phosphatase, deacetylase inhibitor cocktails)
		a. For 3 ml:
		b. 5X IP Low buffer: 600 ul
		c. PIC: 30 ul
		d. Phosphatase: 30 ul
		e. Deacetylase: 30 ul
		f. DTT: 3 ul
		g. Sigma H2O: 2307 ul
	6. 30 ul 1X Laemmli (diluted in 1X IP Wash Low buffer) added to each tube
	7. Tubes boiled at 65C for 5 minutes to elute
	8. Spin and place on magnet
	9. Transfer eluent to fresh 1.5 ml protein lo bind tube
	10. Beta mercaptoethanol added to 5% final v/v
	11. Samples boiled at 95C for 5 minutes

exps.name: DRG Nuclear SMC3 Crosslinked IP 1 (MS 1)
exps.experimentalProtocol:
9.29.25 - Tissue collection

Total DRG collected from 14 male BL6 mice (DOB 7.8.25, 12 weeks old) into two 1.5 ml protein lo-bind tubes, 7 mice each
DRG washed 2X in HBSS, flash frozen in LN2, and stored at -80C

10.1.25 Antibody binding

	1. 1 mg of Dynabeads M-270 epoxy beads weighed into each of two 1.5 ml protein lo-bind Eppendorf tubes
	2. Beads washed 1X in 1 ml of C1
	3. 5 ug of antibody + C1 added to beads
		a. SMC3: 10 ul ab (5 ug, 0.5 ug/ul) + 90 ul C1
		b. IgG: 5 ul ab (5 ug, 1 ug/ul) + 95 ul C1
	4. 100 ul of C2 added to each tube and mixed by gentle pipetting
	5. Bead/antibody mixtures incubated at 37C overnight with shaking

10.2.25 Antibody coupling, nuclear lysate, IP, elution

Bead Preparation
	1. Antibody bound beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
		a. Unbound antibody fraction collected in separate 1.5 ml protein lo bind tubes and stored at 4C
	2. 800 ul of HB (NO tween 20) added to tubes and mixed gently manually
	3. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	4. 800 ul LB (NO tween 20) added to tubes and mixed gently manually
	5. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	6. 800 ul PBS (NO tween 20) added to each tube and mixed gently manually
	7. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	8. An additional 800 ul of PBS (NO tween 20) added to each tube and mixed gently manually
	9. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	10. 800 ul PBS (NO tween 20) added to tubes and mixed gently manually
	11. Beads incubated for 15 minutes at room temp with nutation
	12. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	13. Antibody-coupled beads resuspended in 100 ul PBS (NO tween 20) (100 ul/mg beads) and stored at 4C until use
Nuclear Lysate Preparation
	1. DRG thawed on ice
	2. On ice, add 100 ul of ice-cold 1X Hypotonic Buffer (1:10 10X Hypotonic in Sigma H2O) supplemented with DTT and Detergent (1:1000 dilution of each)
		a. Supplement with anti-protease/phosphatase/deacetylase
	3. Homogenize with mortar and pestle for 15 seconds
	4. Add supplemented 1X Hypotonic Buffer up to 500 ul total volume
	5. Incubate on ice for 15 minutes
	6. Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 850 x g at 4C
	7. Remove supernatant and gently resuspend cell pellet in 1 ml 1X Hypotonic Buffer (no DTT or Detergent) by pipetting up and down several times
	8. Incubate for 15 minutes on ice
	9. Check small aliquot under scope to make sure cells are swollen
	10. Add 50 L Detergent and gently pipette up and down 3-5 times to mix
	11. Centrifuge suspension for 30 seconds at 14,000 x g in a microcentrifuge pre-cooled at 4C
	12. Transfer supernatant (cytoplasmic fraction) to new 1.5 ml protein lo-bind tube. Keep pellet (nuclear fraction) in original tube on ice
	13. Check small aliquot under scope to see if nuclei are released and intact
	14. Resuspend nuclear pellet in 200 L Complete Digestion Buffer by pipetting up and down 3-5 times
		a. Per sample:
		a. 193 ul digestion buffer
		b. 2 ul protease inhibitor cocktail
		c. 2 ul phosphatase inhibitor
		d. 2 ul deacetylase inhibitor
		e. 1 ul PMSF
	15. Add 1 L of the Enzymatic Shearing Cocktail to each sample and vortex gently for 2 seconds
	16. Incubate suspension at 4C for 90 minutes
	17. Add 4 L 0.5 M EDTA to stop the reaction
	18. Vortex gently on a low setting for 2 seconds and place on ice for 5 minutes
	19. Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 14,000 x g in a microcentrifuge pre-cooled at 4C
	20. Transfer supernatant (soluble nuclear fraction) into a pre-chilled 1.5 ml protein lo-bind tube
	21. Determine protein concentration of nuclear soluble fraction via BCA assay
		a. Nuclear lysates pooled, avg conc = 2.56 ug/ul. Total volume ~400 ul
SMC3 Immunoprecipitation
	1. Collected antibody bound beads on magnetic rack and removed antibody solution
	2. Washed beads 3X in 1 ml 1X IP Low buffer (no DTT, PIC)
		a. For 3 ml:
		b. 5X IP Low buffer: 600 ul
		c. Sigma H2O: 2400 ul
	3. Incubated antibody bound beads with 512 ug protein (200 ul) (added at 14:15) for 1 hour at 4 degrees with nutation
		a. Volume brought to 500 ul with 1X IP Incubation Low buffer (+DTT, protease, phosphatase, deacetylase inhibitor cocktails)
		a. For 500 ul:
		a. 5X IP Low buffer: 100 ul
		b. PIC: 5 ul
		c. Phosphatase inhibitor: 5 ul
		d. Deacetylase inhibitor: 5 ul
		e. 1M DTT: 0.5 ul
		f. Sigma H2O: 384.5 ul
	4. Collected beads using a magnetic rack and removed unbound fraction
		a. Unbound fraction stored at 4C for downstream analysis
	5. Washed beads 1 X in 1ml of 1X IP Wash Low buffer (NO DTT, protease, phosphatase, deacetylase inhibitor cocktails)
		a. For 3 ml:
		b. 5X IP Low buffer: 600 ul
		c. Sigma H2O: 2400 ul
	6. Washed beads 2X in 50 mM Tris pH 7.5 (no DTT, inhibitors)
	7. After last wash, add 40 microliters of 0.1M glycine pH 2.5 in milliQ H2O
	8. Tap to resuspend the beads (no pipetting!) and incubate at RT for 3 min
	9. Spin and place on magnet
	10. Transfer eluent to fresh 1.5 ml protein lo bind tube and adjust pH by adding 8 μl of Tris/HCl 1M pH 9.0 in milliQ H2O (1:20)
		a. 1/10th of eluent saved for confirmation of SMC3 enrichment by WB, 9/10ths for MS
		b. Beta mercaptoethanol added to 5% final v/v for WB fractions and samples boiled at 95C for 5 minutes
	11. Tubes spun briefly and stored at 4C

exps.experimentalProtocol:
9.23.25 Antibody binding

	1. 1 mg of Dynabeads M-270 epoxy beads weighed into each of three 1.5 ml protein lo-bind Eppendorf tubes
	2. Beads washed 1X in 1 ml of C1, collected on magnetic rack, and supernatant removed
	3. 5 ug of antibody + C1 added to beads
		a. 2X SMC3: 10 ul ab (5 ug, 0.5 ug/ul) + 90 ul C1 (Bethyl Rb A300-060A, lot 11)
		b. 1X IgG: 5 ul ab (5 ug, 1 ug/ul) + 95 ul C1 (Millipore 12-370, lot 3974804)
		c. NOTE: both antibodies contained glycerol, which is likely to interfere with antibody coupling. May need to get glycerol-free stocks for this application
	4. 100 ul of C2 added to each tube and mixed by gentle pipetting
	5. Bead/antibody mixtures incubated at 37C overnight with nutation
		a. NOTE: may need to buy a heated rotator, this setup isn't really mixing the beads well. Volume too low. Can also move beads to 0.5 ml tubes for ab incubation

9.24.25 Antibody coupling, tissue collection, nuclear lysate, IP

	1. Antibody bound beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
		a. Unbound antibody fraction collected in separate 1.5 ml protein lo bind tubes and stored at 4C
	2. 800 ul of HB + 0.1% tween 20 added to tubes and mixed gently manually
	3. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	4. 800 ul LB + 0.1% tween 20 added to tubes and mixed gently manually
	5. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	6. 800 ul SB added to each tube and mixed gently manually
	7. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	8. An additional 800 ul of SB added to each tube and mixed gently manually
	9. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	10. 800 ul SB added to tubes and mixed gently manually
	11. Beads incubated for 15 minutes at room temp with nutation
	12. Beads collected on magnetic rack and supernatant removed
	13. Antibody-coupled beads resuspended in 100 ul SB (100 ul/mg beads) and stored at 4C until use
	14. ~30 mg of BL6 male cortex placed in each of 3 1.5 ml protein lo bind tubes
	15. 200 ul RIPA + anti protease and phosphatase added to each tube, homogenized with mortar and pestle 15 sec on ice
	16. 300 ul RIPA + anti protease and phosphatase added to each tube and tubes incubated at 4C with nutation for 30 minutes
	17. Centrifuged tubes at 18,000xg for 20 mins at 4 degrees
	18. Ran BCA assay on samples to determine protein concentration
	19. Collected beads on magnetic rack and removed antibody solution
	20. Incubated antibody bound beads with 1.5 mg protein (208.3 ul of pooled lysate, 7.2 ug/ul) for 1 hour at 4 degrees with nutation
	21. Collected beads using a magnetic rack and removed unbound fraction
		a. Unbound fraction stored in fresh 1.5 ml protein lo bind tubes at 4C for downstream analysis
	22. Washed beads 3 x in 1ml of RIPA + anti protease and phosphatase
	23. Elution
		a. SMC3 Laemmli:
		a. Added 50 ul of 1X loading buffer in RIPA lysis buffer (+ anti protease and phosphatase) (NO BETA MERCAPTOETHANOL)
		a. 12.5 ul 4X Laemmli
		b. 35 ul CHAPS lysis buffer (+ anti protease and phosphatase)
		b. Boil 65C for 5 mins
		c. Boiled beads at 95 C for 10 minutes
		b. SMC3 Glycine:
		a. After last wash, add 50 microliters of 0.1M glycine pH 2.5 in milliQ H2O
		b. Tap to resuspend the beads (no pipetting!) and incubate at RT for 3 min
		c. Spin and place on magnet
		d. Recover eluate (without taking beads) and adjust pH by adding 2.5 μl of Tris/HCl 1M pH 9.0 in milliQ H2O (1:20)
		e. Spin and place on magnet, to remove any beads contaminant
		f. Add normal loading buffer
		a. sometimes it may turn yellow, it means that ph is still too acidic, adjust with tiny micro of Tris/HCl 1 M pH 9.0 before loading
		g. Added 10 ul tris/hcl pH 9.0 to titrate
		c. IgG (split half and half glycine and Laemmli elution):
	24. Spun down beads and collected on magnetic rack
	25. Eluent transferred to new tube
	26. Beta mercaptoethanol added to 5% final v/v (2.5 ul for Laemmli samples, 3.34 ul for glycine samples) and samples boiled at 95C for 5 minutes
	27. Tubes spun briefly and stored at 4C

9.25.25 Gel run and primary

	1. Input and FT samples prepared as below
	2. 4-15% TGX gel loaded as below
	3. Gel run started at 40V until samples left wells
	4. Voltage increased 20V every 10 minutes to a final voltage of 100V
	5. Gel run stopped once dye front was just above bottom of cassette
	6. Gel transferred to PVDF membrane using transblot turbo buffer, high MW protocol
	7. Membrane blocked in 5% milk 0.2% PBST at RT with shaking for 1 hour
	8. Primary antibody dilutions added
		a. SMC3: 1:500 Rabbit polyclonal, Bethyl laboratories A300-060A, lot 11

9.28.25 NIPBL primary

	1. NIPBL: 1:1000 Rb (Novus NBP1-85110, lot A106772)

exps.experimentalProtocol:
12.3.25 DRG Collection

Total DRG collected from 5 male BL6 mice (DOB 8.15.25) and 1 male BL6 mouse (DOB 9.2.25), 2 mice per tube
DRG washed 1X with cold, sterile HBSS
HBSS aspirated and DRG flash frozen in LN2, stored at -80C

12.4.25 Nuclei and RNA isolation

Nuclei isolation from mouse DRG
A pool of total DRG from 2 mice/tube.
IMPORTANT: nuclei tend to clump, so they need to be always diluted and BSA added in the buffers to avoid clumping and increase centrifugation efficiency
BSA is also important to avoid nuclei sticking to the plastic Eppendorf walls. Coat the Eppi and falcon tubes with 1 %BSA for few hours. BSA 1%: 0.15 g BSA (Jackson Immuno Research 001-000-162) in 15 ml molecular biology water
	Per sample:
	4 2 ml DNA lo bind eppendorf
	2 50 ml falcons
	Total:
	12 2 ml DNA lo bind eppendorf
	6 50 ml falcons
	BSA solution:
	1 ml per eppendorf
	10 ml per falcon
	72 ml total
	Prep 80 ml
	80 ml mol bio H2O
	0.8 g mol bio grade BSA
	Tubes coated overnight at room temp on rotating wheel
Homogenization buffer 50 ml
Filter before addition of RNase inhibitor.
Take an aliquot of 1 ml before adding TritonX100.
All steps were performed on ice or in the cold room, and all incubations were carried out using an end-to-end rotator.
HB prep started @ 11:30
Nuclei isolation started @ 12:00
	1. Coat the Eppendorf and falcon tubes with 1% BSA for 3+ hours
	2. DRGs are removed from dry ice and placed into 100 ul of homogenization buffer w/o Triton
	3. After a brief incubation on ice, the samples were homogenized using the blue pellet pestle for 15 sec
	4. A 10% Triton-X100 (Sigma) solution was added to a final concentration of 0.1% (1.1 ul) and additional strokes with the blue pestle were performed for an additional 15 sec.
	5. Add homogenization buffer plus Triton 0.1% washing the pestle with 700 ul/tube and pipette up and down. Split each sample in 2 tubes 350 ul/each. Let the clumps settle and filter the supernatant through a 70-μm filter.
	6. Add 100 ul of homogenization buffer/ 0.1% Triton to the clump pellet and additional strokes with the blue pestle were performed for extra 15 sec.
	7. Add homogenization buffer/Triton 0.1% washing the pestle up to 700 ul/tube
	8. Pipette up and down and let the clumps settle
	9. Pass homogenate through a 70-μm filter and pool with the previous one.
	10. Repeat the procedure another time for the remaining clumps.
	11. Finally, wash filter with additional 200 ul homogenization buffer/0.1% Triton and recover all the liquid at the bottom of the strainer
	12. Filter again with a 40-μm filter and recover all the liquid at the bottom of the strainer.
	13. Check the final volume (aim to resuspend all the nuclei from 2 mice in 4 ml).
	14. Take 40 microliters (10%) aliquot as negative unstained control for the sorting and add 300 microliters of homogenization buffer/Triton (keep on ice until needed)
	15. Split the 4 ml in 2 Eppendorf tubes of 2 ml/each and add MAB377X clone A60 LOT NUMBER: 3782109 1.0 mg/mL to appropriate dilution
		a. 1:100 (20 ul)
		b. 1:500 (4 ul)
		c. 1:1000 (2 ul)
	16. Incubate 30 minutes in the cold room, rotating.
	Labeling done @ 14:00
	17. Centrifuge at 1100 g at 4C for 10 min. Remove sv.
	18. Wash 3x in 2 ml of homogenization buffer/Triton/2%BSA, removing sv each time.
	19. After last wash, resuspend in 2 ml homogenization buffer/triton/2% BSA
	20. Filter through 30 um sieve
	21. Split into 2 2ml tubes
	22. Spin 1100 g at 4C for 10 min
	23. Remove supernatant and resuspend each pellet in 80 ul buffer
	24. To one tube of each antibody concentration, add 1 ul donkey anti-mouse Fab blocking reagent and incubate at 4C for 10 minutes
	25. To all tubes, add 20 ul anti-mouse IgG MicroBeads per 10^7 nuclei
	26. Mix well, incubate for 15 minutes at 4C (in fridge)
	Bead binding done @ 16:05
	27. Wash nuclei by adding 1 ml buffer and centrifuge at 1200xg for 10 minutes at 4C
	28. Remove supernatant
	29. Resuspend pellet in 1 ml buffer
	30. Place LS column on magnetic rack
	31. Rinse column with 1 ml buffer (PBS + 0.5% BSA)
	32. Apply nuclei/bead suspension to column
	33. Collect flow through in 15ml tube
	34. Wash column with 1 ml buffer 3X and collect flow through in same 15 ml tube
	35. Remove column from magnetic rack and place over 2 ml DNA lo bind tube
	36. Apply 1ml buffer to tube and flush with plunger, collecting bound fraction
	37. Place new LS column on magnetic rack
	38. Rinse column with 1 ml buffer
	39. Apply bound fraction from first column to new column
	40. Collect flow through in original 15ml tube
	41. Wash column with 1 ml buffer 3X and collect flow through in same 15 ml tube
	42. Remove column from magnetic rack and place over 2 ml DNA lo bind tube
	43. Apply 1ml buffer to tube and flush with plunger, collecting bound fraction
	44. Aliquot 1/10th of each eluent fraction sample into 1.5 ml protein lo bind tube for BCA assay
		a. Lyse in 100 ul RIPA + anti-protease by vortexing for 30 seconds
		b. Proceed with BCA protocol after RNA isolation
	45. Spin 2 ml tubes (for RNA) at 1200 g 4C for 10 minutes
	46. Pre-warm centrifuge to room temp
	47. Remove supernatant and resuspend each pellet in 350 ul buffer RLT + 1% beta-mercaptoethanol
		a. For n = 8
		b. 2800 ul RLT
		c. 28 ul BME
	48. Vortex samples for 30 seconds
	49. Proceed with RNeasy micro kit protocol for RNA isolation
RNA Isolation
All spins must be performed at room temp (at or above 20C)
	1. Add 350 ul of 70% ethanol to lysate, mix well by pipetting
	2. Transfer sample to RNeasy column in a 2 ml collection tube
	3. Close lid and centrifuge for 15 seconds at >8000 x g
	4. Discard flow through
	5. Add 350 ul buffer RW1 to column, close lid, and centrifuge for 15 seconds at >8000 x g
	6. Discard flow through
	7. Add 10 ul DNase I stock solution to 70 ul buffer RDD
		a. Prepare 8x volume
		b. 80 ul Dnase I + 560 ul buffer RDD
	8. Mix by gently inverting tube (DO NOT VORTEX) and add 80 ul DNase I incubation mix directly to column membrane
	9. Incubate column in DNase I for 15 minutes at room temp
	10. Add 350 ul buffer RW1 to column, close lid, spin for 15 seconds at >8000 x g
	11. Discard collection tube
	12. Place column into new 2 ml collection tube and add 500 ul buffer RPE to column, close lid, spin for 15 seconds at >8000 x g
	13. Discard flow through
	14. Add 500 ul 80% ethanol to column, close lid, spin for 2 minutes at >8000 x g
	15. Discard collection tube
	16. Place column in new 2 ml collection tube, open lid, centrifuge at full speed for 5 minutes to dry membrane
	17. Discard flow through and collection tube
	18. Place column in new 1.5 ml collection tube
	19. Add 14 ul RNase-free water directly to center of membrane and let stand for 1 minute
	20. Close lid and centrifuge at full speed for 1 minute to elute RNA
	21. Prepare 1 aliquot of 2 ul of resulting RNA solution for tapestation analysis
	22. Flash freeze samples in LN2, store at -80C

1.10.26 RT-PCR

RT PCR
SuperScript II First-Strand Synthesis System for RT-PCR (invitrogen 18080-051)
1 pg - 5 ug of total RNA or 1 pg - 500 ng of poly(A)+ RNA starting material
	1. Mix and briefly centrifuge each component prior to use
	2. Combine the following in a 0.2 or 0.5 ml tube per sample
		a. Up to 5 ug total RNA (x ul)
		b. Primers
		a. 50 uM oligo(dT) (1 ul)
		b. Random hexamer (1 ul)
		c. 10 mM dNTP mix (1 ul)
		d. DEPC H2O (to 10.5 ul)
	3. Incubate tube at 65C for 5 min
	4. Place tube on ice for at least 1 min
	5. Prepare cDNA synthesis mix (add each component IN ORDER)
		a. 10X RT buffer (2.1 ul)
		b. 25 mM MgCl2 (4.2 ul)
		c. 0.1 M DTT (2.1 ul)
		d. RNaseOUT (40 U/ul) (1.05 ul)
		e. SuperScript III RT (200 U/ul) (1.05 ul)
	6. Add 10.5 ul (or RNA + primer volume, if adjusted) cDNA synthesis mix to each RNA/primer mixture
		a. NOTE: +RT master mix ran out after first 10 samples, fresh master mix prepared for 1000 block and 1000 block FT
	7. Mix gently and collect by centrifugation
	8. Incubate at 25C for 10 min
	9. Incubate at 50C for 50 min
	10. Terminate reaction at 85C for 5 min
	11. Chill on ice
	12. Collect reactions by brief centrifugation
	13. Add 1 ul of RNase H to each tube and incubate at 37C for 20 min
	14. cDNA can be stored at -20C or used for PCR immediately

1.11.26 qPCR

qPCR for TUJI, SOX10, GAPDH
0.5 ug RNA in 20 ul RT reaction volume
Dilute 1:5
	final concentration 0.5 ug/100 ul (5 ng/ul)
	If less input RNA, adjust dilution to reach same final cDNA concentration, if possible
	1. Thaw, thoroughly mix, and centrifuge all components. Store protected from light
	2. Prepare master reaction mixture as follows
	3. Thoroughly mix master mix and dispense equal aliquots into each well of a qPCR plate
	4. Add DNA samples to wells
	5. Seal plate with optically transparent film and vortex for 30s
	6. Spin plate to remove air bubbles (pop with needle if necessary)
Primer product sizes
Tuji: 88 bp
Sox10: 586 bp
2-3% agarose
Run 10 ul per sample, one rep from each condition/target pair

	Gently resuspend ConA beads and transfer 11 μL per reaction to a 1.5 mL tube.
	Place tube on a magnet, allow slurry to clear. Pipette to remove supernatant.

	Repeat the previous step one time.
	Resuspend beads in 11 μL per reaction cold Bead Activation Buffer.
	Aliquot 10 μL per reaction of bead slurry into 8-strip tubes. Place on ice.
	CUT&RUN Binding Cells to Activated Beads (30 min)
	Count starting cells and confirm integrity. Harvest 500,000 cells per reaction (plus 10% excess) and spin at 600 x g for 3 min at RT. Remove supernatant.

	Remove tubes from magnet. Immediately add 50 L cold Antibody Buffer to each reaction and pipette to resuspend. Confirm ConA bead binding (Appendix 1.2).

	Remove tubes from 4˚C incubation and quick spin to collect liquid. Note that beads may settle overnight - this is normal and will not impact results.

	Repeat the previous step one time (keep tubes on magnet).
	Remove tubes from magnet and immediately add 50 μL cold Cell Permeabilization Buffer to each reaction. Gently vortex and/or pipette with a P200 to mix.

	Incubate reactions for 10 min at RT.

	Add 420 μL DNA Binding Buffer to each reaction. Mix well by vortexing.
	For every CUT&RUN reaction, place a DNA Cleanup Column into a DNA Collection Tube. Load each reaction onto a column and label the top.
	Spin at 16,000 x g, 30 sec, RT. Discard flow-through. Place column back into collection tube.
	Add 200 μL DNA Wash Buffer to each column. Spin at 16,000 x g, 30 sec, RT. Discard flow-through. Place column back into collection tube.
	Repeat previous step one time.
	Spin at 16,000 x g, 30 sec, RT to completely dry the column.
	Carefully remove the column from the collection tube, ensuring it does not contact the flow-through. Transfer column to a clean pre-labeled 1.5 mL tube.
	Add 12 μL DNA Elution Buffer, taking care to ensure the buffer is added to the center of the column rather than the wall. Tap the column & microfuge collection tube on the benchtop to ensure all droplets are absorbed onto the resin. * DNA can be eluted in 6–20 μL; 12 µL is recommended. Larger elution volumes, longer incubation times, and/or multiple rounds of elution may improve DNA yield. However, DNA concentration will be reduced with larger elution volume.

	1. Thaw kit reagents stored at -20˚C and keep on ice (4˚C) during the experiment.
	2. Transfer 5 ng of CUT&RUN-enriched DNA to a new 8-strip tube and adjust final volume to 25 L with 0.1X TE Buffer. For CUT&RUN reactions with yields below 5 ng DNA, use as much DNA as possible for library prep.
	3. Prepare an End Repair Master Mix for N reactions by combining the following reagents in a fresh 1.5 mL tube on ice.
